children: Japan's Nikkei share average rebounded sharply on Thursday from near its lowest level since April, as investors snapped up AI-focused stocks following steep declines.

rose 1.6% to 57,902.41 by 0158 GMT, after gaining more than 2% earlier. It had fallen as low as 56,502.97 on Wednesday, just above Friday's low of 56,436.65, which was its weakest level since April 13.
surged 12.1%, making it the Nikkei's biggest percentage gainer. The stock slumped more than 14% on Wednesday and touched a nearly eight-month low.
soared more than 10%, after plunging nearly 15% on Wednesday to its lowest level since July last year.
Heavily weighted chip-testing tool maker Advantest
climbed 6.3% and contributed 324 points to the Nikkei's 890-point gain, making it the index's biggest points contributor.

"It is important to remain mindful that AI-related shares are likely to continue their stop-and-go movement, with dip-buying occurring when prices fall and selling resuming once they have recovered to a certain extent," said Wataru Akiyama, a strategist at Nomura Securities.
"Concerns regarding the sustainability of AI-related investments have not been dispelled."
The Nikkei has seesawed this week amid leadership turmoil at AI bellwether Nvidia
and worries that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections earlier this month could slow AI infrastructure development.
The index jumped 3.9% on Tuesday after slumping 5.1% on Friday. Japanese markets were closed on Monday for a holiday.
On Thursday, of the Nikkei's 225 components, 185 advanced, 38 declined and two were unchanged.
